notes: Correction from the previous version: the parts list has one 220 ohm resistor, so I removed the other three and kept one (r1).

The single resistor sits in the shared ground return, between the MKR GND wire and the breadboard ground rail. Both the white LED cathode and the RGB common cathode go to that rail, so all LED current passes through it. This is my reading, because the schematic image was not readable and the text does not say where the resistor goes.
The sketch sets the pins: pin 5 drives the white LED, and pins 2, 3 and 4 drive RGB red, blue and green. The signal wires go straight to the LED legs through the breadboard.

The ENV shield stacks on the MKR WiFi 1010 (joined edge). Its headers pass the board's pins through, so the wires attach to the MKR board's own pin ports. Its temperature sensor is on-board and needs no extra wiring.
The catalogue lookup for the MKR ENV Shield returned the wrong part (MKR Relay Proto Shield), so arduino-mkr-env-shield is a new type with port names I chose.
The breadboard column numbers, and the LED legs going directly into the ground rail, are my own layout.
The Alexa app, Arduino Cloud and Cloud Editor are software only and are not nodes.
